turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (NURSE): Morning. Pop your arm out and I'll get the blood pressure and temperature done before you go in.
[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): Of course. Thank you very much.
[SEG0003] person_1 (NURSE): That's 146 over 84, pulse 78, temperature 36.7. You're all set.
[SEG0004] person_3 (CAREGIVER): I'll come through with him, if that's allowed. My sister's pregnant, about seven months, and I've been a bit wound up about anything catching.
[SEG0005] person_4 (DOCTOR): Sorry, uh, the screen's gone again. One moment. Right. What can I do for you?
[SEG0006] person_2 (PATIENT): Good morning, doctor. Forgive me for taking up your time. I have a burning pain on one side of my chest, and a few blisters have appeared.
[SEG0007] person_4 (DOCTOR): Sorry, say that once more, I was clicking the wrong tab.
[SEG0008] person_2 (PATIENT): A burning pain, on the left side of my chest. And several small blisters. It has been going on for two days.
[SEG0009] person_4 (DOCTOR): Two days. Umm. Are the blisters in a sort of stripe?
[SEG0010] person_2 (PATIENT): Yes, doctor. They form a little band, from under the shoulder blade round to the front. They have not crossed to the other side.
[SEG0011] person_3 (CAREGIVER): The shirt sets it off. He winces when the cloth rubs.
[SEG0012] person_4 (DOCTOR): Mm. Have you felt feverish? Hot, or shivery?
[SEG0013] person_2 (PATIENT): No, doctor. I have not felt feverish.
[SEG0014] person_4 (DOCTOR): Any cough? Or shortness of breath?
[SEG0015] person_2 (PATIENT): No. My breathing has been quite ordinary.
[SEG0016] person_4 (DOCTOR): Did you ever have chickenpox?
[SEG0017] person_2 (PATIENT): Yes. Well, I had chickenpox as a child. I was seven, I believe, or perhaps eight.
[SEG0018] person_4 (DOCTOR): Let me see. Yes. There is a cluster of small blisters on a red base on the left side of the chest, and it stops at the midline. The right side is clear.
[SEG0019] person_2 (PATIENT): I do hope it is nothing too grave.

[SEG0020] person_4 (DOCTOR): I think this is shingles. The old chickenpox virus sits in the nerve root, and it travels back out along that one nerve. That is why the burning and the blisters stay in a stripe.
[SEG0021] person_3 (CAREGIVER): Oh dear. My sister actually had a bout like that years back, before this pregnancy. Ought he to keep away from her?

[SEG0022] person_4 (DOCTOR): Yes. Until those blisters crust, stay away from her. If she isn't immune she can catch chickenpox from the blister fluid, and that isn't good in pregnancy. No shared towels, and wash your hands.
[SEG0023] person_2 (PATIENT): I quite understand. I shall keep well clear of her.

[SEG0024] person_4 (DOCTOR): I'll start an antiviral today. Valaciclovir, one gram, three times a day, for seven days. The box on screen has come up as vala-cyclo-vir, ignore that, it's the same medicine. Begin this afternoon.
[SEG0025] person_2 (PATIENT): Valaciclovir, one gram, three times a day, for seven days. Thank you.
[SEG0026] person_4 (DOCTOR): What else are you taking? The medication page won't load. Say it again for me.
[SEG0027] person_2 (PATIENT): Only amlodipine, five milligrams by mouth, once every morning, for my blood pressure. I also took paracetamol yesterday, two tablets, twice, for the burning.
[SEG0028] person_4 (DOCTOR): Amlodipine 5 milligrams once a day, yes, carry on. Paracetamol is all right, up to two tablets four times a day if the pain needs it.
[SEG0029] person_3 (CAREGIVER): He missed the morning amlodipine once or twice last week. I couldn't say he's had every single dose.
[SEG0030] person_4 (DOCTOR): Right. Try not to miss it. Err. If the burning hasn't settled in two weeks we might arrange a scan, but not today.
[SEG0031] person_2 (PATIENT): Very well. Would you like to see me again?

[SEG0032] person_4 (DOCTOR): Yes. I'll see you here in one week, to check it's crusting. If the pain gets into the eye, or you feel properly unwell before then, come sooner, don't wait on the appointment.
[SEG0033] person_2 (PATIENT): Thank you, doctor. That is very clear.
[SEG0034] person_1 (NURSE): Prescription will be at reception. Mind how you go.

spec.situation: Older person with burning pain on one side of the chest and a few blisters for two days; remembers chickenpox as a child; doctor prescribes antiviral today and gives infection advice about contact with a pregnant relative.

traps.happens: The doctor (or nurse) explains a mechanism or a diagnosis in the patient's body ('the voice box is irritated by reflux', 'diabetes dulls the nerves in the feet', 'the swelling is your body fighting infection'). A nurse or caregiver also mentions a fact about THEIR OWN life (their sister, their child, their own illness).
traps.label_rule: Explanations by the doctor are NEVER symptoms, history or social history of the patient; they may only appear as clinical_assessment or counselling if the doctor stated them as such. A nurse's or caregiver's own life facts are not recorded as the patient's. Each symptom's reported_by is the person who really described it.

features: hedged_plan: the doctor hedges ('we might do a scan if it does not settle', 'let's see in two weeks'). Conditional vs planned status must follow the words.
doctor_misses_topics: the doctor does not ask about everything; topics never discussed are simply absent (no invented denials, no allergy line if allergies were never mentioned).
spec.doctor_style: distracted by the computer, asks for repeats

bad.reason: Taken yesterday for burning is supported; 'currently_used' is not clearly stated.
bad.text: paracetamol (dose=2 tablets, frequency=twice yesterday, indication=burning pain, status=currently_used, reported_by=patient)

bad.reason: Avoid her, no shared towels, wash hands supported; transcript says pregnant sister, not generic pregnant woman.
bad.text: Stay away from the pregnant woman until the blisters crust, do not share towels, and wash hands (action_type=counselling, status=recommended, responsible_person=patient)

omissions.text: Past history of chickenpox in childhood (age about 7 or 8).
Rash/blisters are unilateral and do not cross the midline/other side, described by the patient as a band from under the left shoulder blade round to the front.

Doctor advised to come sooner if the pain gets into the eye or if the patient feels properly unwell before the 1-week review; the recorded follow-up incorrectly says 'pain gets into the eye' rather than the shingles/rash being in or near the eye.
